title: Does a searched posture let a Unitree G1 hold a stud longer than the default pose?
summary: buildbot-holdheat found the G1 waist at 0.54 of peak torque with empty hands at the stud-carry pose and 0.91 with a 3.8 kg stud. The arms are redundant for a fixed hand position and the centre of pressure can move along the foot, so this searches both in MuJoCo (random anchors then a (1+1) evolution strategy, self-collision rejected, three seeds, best kept). With the centre of pressure 3 cm inside the toe edge the default posture gives 0.744 and the best searched posture 0.487 (other seeds 0.63 and 0.68, so the search is noisy and 0.487 is an upper bound on the minimum); a continuous rating of 0.5 of peak then makes the stud sustainable. With the centre of pressure on the sole point the gain is 0.910 to 0.756; at the toe edge 0.586. A 2x6 goes 0.93 to 0.68; sheet, block and drywall cases stay above peak. For a continuous rating of 0.4 or less nothing is sustainable at this pose. Static only; the continuous rating and thermal time constant remain unsourced (swept), the toe edge is read from the model, and the search is weak.
lede: does a searched arm and waist posture let a G1 hold a stud longer? In MuJoCo the stud's peak joint fraction falls from 0.91 (default) to 0.76 with the centre of pressure on the sole point and to 0.49 (best of three noisy seeds) 3 cm inside the toe edge, enough to make a stud sustainable at a continuous rating of 0.5 of peak; a 2x6 goes 0.93 to 0.68 and sheets stay above peak.
